title: Geometry of Love
label: EastWest · Aero Productions
overview:
Jarre's fifteenth studio album, commissioned by Jean-Roch as the soundtrack for the chill-out area of his VIP Room nightclub in Paris and released in 2003 on EastWest (catalogue 2564 60693-2); the sleeve reads "Project by Jarre for VIP Room". The first run was planned as 2,000 copies sold at the club's wardrobe, and Jarre's own site says the music was meant to be played in the background rather than listened to head-on. Discogs lists Joachim Garraud as mixer, David Perreau as mastering engineer, Francis Rimbert as artistic collaborator and Patrick Pelamourgues as technical assistant, none of them credited on the sleeve; the cover is a pixelated photograph of the actress Isabelle Adjani, processed by Ora-Ïto. The fan site Aerozone JMJ lists the equipment for this album and Sessions 2000 together: ARP 2600, Eminent 310 U, EMS Synthi AKS, EMS VCS 3, Minimoog, RMI Harmonic Synthesizer, Korg Karma, Korg microKORG, Korg Mini Pops 7, Novation Supernova II, Roland JP-8000, Roland XP-80, Roland HandSonic, E-mu XL7, the Geiss Digisequencer and Pro Tools. Wikipedia places it closer to Sessions 2000 (2002) than to Jarre's earlier albums, but more electronica than jazz, and notes that some of its sounds were used earlier on Interior Music (2001).

The album issued no singles, and Aerozone JMJ says it passed almost unnoticed; no chart position is documented. The physical CD was long out of print, and a remastered CD reissue from Columbia and Sony Music followed in 2018. The title track is split in two parts that frame the album at tracks 2 and 8. Six of the eight pieces have a steady beat for most of their length, "Soul Intrusion" holds its beat back until the middle, and "Near Djaina" has no steady beat at all.

Section timestamps are measured on a CD rip and are approximate to ±5 seconds.

tracks.title: Pleasure Principle
tracks.role: Album role: The opening track and the album's second-longest, a near-silent start that builds into a long, steady groove.

events.description: A very quiet, beatless opening with almost no low end.
events.detail: Wikipedia and Jarre's site describe the album as lounge music for the chill-out area of the VIP Room club, to be played in the background.

events.description: The bass arrives and the level jumps: the biggest change in the track.
The bass drops out and a clearer pulse leads for about 20 seconds.
The low end returns and the groove builds, with a short dip at 1:25.
The sub-bass grows and the track settles into its fullest stretch, which runs with a few short breaks to about 5:20.
The level dips for about 20 seconds, with the highs cut at first, before the full groove returns at 3:55.
The top end cuts briefly and the arrangement thins for the closing half-minute.
The level drops and the track fades out by 6:08.

tracks.title: Geometry of Love, Part 1
tracks.role: Album role: The first half of the two-part title track and the album's shortest piece, with a beat from the first seconds.

events.description: The bass and a steady beat arrive within five seconds.
A brighter layer joins on top and the highs open.
The highs recede for about 20 seconds while the beat carries on.
The top end opens again and stays open to about 2:20: the brightest stretch of the track, with the firmest beat from 1:50.
The highs and the bass thin out for about ten seconds.
The full arrangement returns, and the highs open again at 3:02.
The highs fall away and the track fades out by 3:44.

tracks.title: Soul Intrusion
tracks.role: Album role: A bass-led piece that holds its beat back until the middle, placed after the two opening beat-led tracks.

events.description: A soft, dark opening with the bass already present.
The sub-bass swells and the low end gains weight over the next ten seconds.
A deeper sub-bass layer enters and the texture fills out, still without a steady beat.
A steady beat enters with a brighter top end: the biggest change in the track and its loudest stretch.
The beat stops, the level drops and the track fades out by 4:38.

tracks.title: Electric Flesh
tracks.role: Album role: A bass-led build in which the beat enters after one minute and two short breakdowns split the second half.

events.description: A beatless, bass-led opening whose level swells and dips in a slow cycle.
A beat enters with a strong sub-bass.
The low end falls back for about 15 seconds before returning at 2:26.
The beat pulls back and the level falls for about half a minute, then rebuilds from 3:31.
The bass and mids drop out for about 15 seconds while the highs stay.
The beat returns with a brighter top end.
The full arrangement returns at its fullest level and runs to the end.
The track ends with a short fade of about five seconds.

tracks.title: Skin Paradox
tracks.role: Album role: The longest track on the album, with its deepest drop in level in the middle and the sharpest return after it.

events.description: A soft opening with the low end present from the start while the highs open within the first 20 seconds.
The sub-bass falls out for about ten seconds and a clearer pulse takes over, then returns at 0:39.
The highs rise and the level steps up to the loudest stretch of the first half around 1:55.
The highs and the beat fall away to the quietest point of the track at about 2:30.
The full arrangement returns in one step, the biggest change in the track, with its steadiest beat from about 2:55; a loud stretch runs from 3:50 to 4:45 after a short dip.
The highs drop out for about 15 seconds.
The full band returns for the last minute, with a short dip at 5:35.
The track fades out by 6:10.

tracks.title: Velvet Road
tracks.role: Album role: A remake of "Children of Space", written for the Rendez-Vous in Space concert in Okinawa in 2001, and the last beat-led track before the beatless "Near Djaina".

events.description: A steady beat and the bass start within the first seconds.
events.detail: Wikipedia names "Children of Space" as an unreleased piece Jarre composed for the Rendez-Vous in Space concert in Okinawa in 2001.

events.description: A brighter layer enters and the level rises.
The sub-bass and the highs fall away and the beat stops for about 20 seconds.
The sub-bass and the beat return, and the highs lift again from 2:50.
The bass drops back and the highs thin out until about 4:15.
The bass returns with a bright top end, and the arrangement holds to the end.
The level drops and the track fades out by 5:48.

tracks.title: Near Djaina
tracks.role: Album role: The album's one track without a steady beat, a quiet interlude between "Velvet Road" and the closing title-track Part 2.

events.description: A soft, dark opening with the bass present from the first seconds and no beat.
The level dips for a few seconds, then lifts at 0:45 as the highs open: the biggest change in the track.
The highs recede and the texture quietens until about 1:35.
The sub-bass swells and the level rises, with a second swell at 2:15.
The texture stays at an even level through the middle, with the highs coming and going.
The highs lift and a faint pulse appears for about ten seconds.
The level falls and the track fades out by 4:55.

tracks.title: Geometry of Love, Part 2
tracks.role: Album role: The closing track and second half of the title track, which mirrors Part 1 with a beat from the first seconds and a short break near the midpoint, then a fade over its last half-minute.

events.description: The bass and a steady beat are present from the first seconds.
The highs lift and the arrangement brightens.
The top end opens further and the beat is at its firmest until about 2:05.
The beat and the highs thin out for about ten seconds.
The full arrangement returns, and the highs lift again from 2:35.
The level falls gradually and the album fades out by about 4:00.
